flagship.headline: Ed Sullivan sees Beatlemania at Heathrow
flagship.summary_line_1: Ed Sullivan, at London Heathrow on October 31, 1963, saw screaming fans greet the Beatles home from Sweden, per This Day in Music.
flagship.summary_line_2: He decided to look into booking them for his American television show, and the clip below is She Loves You.

events.headline: Apple releases the Beatles' Something / Come Together in the UK
events.summary_line_1: Apple released the Beatles' double A-side single Something / Come Together (Apple R 5814) in the UK on October 31, 1969, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It peaked at No. 4 on the UK chart, and the clip below is Something.

events.headline: MC5 record the second night of Kick Out the Jams in Detroit
events.summary_line_1: MC5 recorded the second night of their live debut album Kick Out the Jams at the Grande Ballroom in Detroit on October 31, 1968, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: Elektra released the album in February 1969 with Jac Holzman and Bruce Botnick producing, and the clip below is the title track.

events.headline: The Stooges play their first show at a Halloween party
events.summary_line_1: The Stooges, then billed as the Psychedelic Stooges, made their live debut at a Halloween party in Ann Arbor, Michigan, on October 31, 1967, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: Their next live gig did not come until January 1968, and the clip below is I Wanna Be Your Dog from their 1969 debut album.

events.headline: Brian Jones is freed from prison on bail
events.summary_line_1: Brian Jones of the Rolling Stones was released from Wormwood Scrubs on bail pending appeal on October 31, 1967, a day after his nine-month sentence for drug possession, per This Day in Music.
events.summary_line_2: A London appeals court overturned the sentence on December 12, 1967, and the clip below is the Stones' 1967 single We Love You.

events.headline: Adam Horovitz of the Beastie Boys is born
events.summary_line_1: Adam Horovitz, who performs as Ad-Rock in the Beastie Boys, was born in South Orange, New Jersey, on October 31, 1966, per Apple TV.
events.summary_line_2: The Beastie Boys were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2012, and the clip below is their single Sabotage.

events.headline: The Supremes hit No. 1 with Baby Love
events.summary_line_1: The Supremes' Baby Love reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on the chart dated October 31, 1964, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It held the top spot for four chart weeks as the second of five straight Supremes No. 1s, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: Barbra Streisand hits No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with People
events.summary_line_1: Barbra Streisand's album People reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 on the chart dated October 31, 1964, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It ended the Beatles' 14-week run at the top with A Hard Day's Night and stayed No. 1 for five weeks, and the clip below is the title song.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Gaumont in Ipswich
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Gaumont Cinema in Ipswich on October 31, 1964, the 18th date of their 1964 British tour, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their second and final visit to Ipswich, and the clip below is their 1964 single A Hard Day's Night.

events.headline: Ed Sullivan sees Beatlemania at Heathrow
events.summary_line_1: Ed Sullivan, at London Heathrow on October 31, 1963, saw screaming fans greet the Beatles home from Sweden, per This Day in Music.
events.summary_line_2: He decided to look into booking them for his American television show, and the clip below is She Loves You.

events.headline: Gerry and the Pacemakers hit UK No. 1 with You'll Never Walk Alone
events.summary_line_1: Gerry and the Pacemakers' You'll Never Walk Alone reached No. 1 on the UK singles chart on October 31, 1963, per This Day in Music.
events.summary_line_2: It was the Liverpool group's third and final UK No. 1, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: Larry Mullen Jr. of U2 is born in Dublin
events.summary_line_1: Larry Mullen Jr., the drummer of U2, was born in Artane, Dublin, on October 31, 1961, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: He would be a founding member of U2, and the clip below is the band's 1980 single I Will Follow.
